case.case_title: Dhammiaka Yapa v. Bandaranayake and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. 110/87, decided on 17 November 1987

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the preventive detention orders under Emergency Regulations violated Article 13(4) by constituting punishment without trial.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that the detention under Regulation 17(1) was punitive and thus violated Article 13(4).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued that preventive detention is not punishment and Regulation 17(1) is constitutionally valid.
key_facts: Wijesekera was detained under Regulation 19(2) for investigation and subsequently under Regulation 17(1) for preventive detention.
The detention under Regulation 17(1) was to prevent him from acting prejudicially to national security and public order.
The petitioner challenged Regulation 17(1) as ultra vires the Constitution and violative of Article 13(4).
The court considered precedents and legal principles distinguishing preventive detention from punishment.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(4) prohibits punishment except by competent court but detention pending investigation or trial is not punishment. Preventive detention under Regulation 17(1) is a precautionary measure, not punitive.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Applying established legal principles and precedents, the court found Regulation 17(1) valid and not in violation of Article 13(4). The detention was preventive, aimed at national security and public order.
principles_established: Preventive detention is qualitatively different from punitive detention.
Detention pending investigation or trial does not constitute punishment under Article 13(4).
Regulation 17(1) of Emergency Regulations is constitutionally valid and not ultra vires.
precedents_cited: Vijaya Kumaranatunga v. G. V. P. Samarasinghe and others

outcome.holding: The court upheld the validity of Regulation 17(1) and held that preventive detention under it does not violate Article 13(4).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) protects against punishment without trial. The court's reasoning on preventive detention under Regulation 17(1) directly addresses this protection and confirms the constitutionality of such detention.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court cited precedents and held that preventive detention is not punishment; Regulation 17(1) is a precautionary measure valid under the Constitution.
